paper text.text: The triangle completion of $B_b$ is three-connected by Lemma~\ref{lem:triangle-completion}, since $D_b-b$ is a component of $G-\{b,c,w\}$. It is a minor of $G$, using the internally disjoint paths $bpc$, $bqap'w$ and $cq'w$ for $bc,bw,cw$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. While $D_b$ keeps its neighbors at $c,w$, the four tests depend on $B_b$ only through $B_b+cw+bw$ and $B_b+cw+bc$. Replacing $B_b$ by a proper allowed minor gives an allowed minor of $B$, since its interior stays adjacent to $w$, the vertices $a,c$ keep $p',q'$, and $d$ keeps $w$. By minimality, no such minor keeps both completions nonplanar. Lemma~\ref{core:two-cap-critical}, with $c,w,b$ as $x,y,z$, therefore makes $B_b$ either $Q(b;c,w)$ or one of the two four-cycle forms. The enumeration~\supp{E15} applies Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} after identifying $c,w$ to a vertex $x$, with attachments $b,x$ and added edge $bx$. It then splits $x$ back into $c,w$, assigning each original edge at $x$ to one of them and adding an edge to an interior vertex at whichever has no interior neighbor. With $\Psi_2$, $p',q'$ and $dw$, the three forms above are among its $24$ candidates. Each has a separating set of at most two vertices or a proper nontoroidal minor.

vertex names: Psi_2: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,b,d}, as in Section 5. Further vertices with these neighbourhoods are p3, ... and r3, .... Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... Twins p', q' have neighbourhood {a,c,w}, as in Section 5.4.3.
